answers.stem_only: Give the HTTPS subscription (not the topic) a redrive policy with an Amazon SQS dead-letter queue. The DLQ must be a standard queue (standard topic) in the same account and Region as the subscription, and its queue policy must let the SNS topic send messages. Undelivered events land there after SNS retries run out and can be replayed later. Longer retry policies do not help: HTTP/S retries are capped well below several hours of outage handling and do not store events.

An Amazon EventBridge rule on the default event bus that matches the EC2 Instance State-change Notification event with state 'stopped'. Targets: the existing Lambda function and an SNS topic with an email subscription. This catches every stop source (console, scripts, schedules) with no polling and no custom code.

Turn on partial batch responses: set FunctionResponseTypes to ReportBatchItemFailures on the SQS event source mapping and have the function return batchItemFailures with the message IDs that failed. Lambda then deletes the successful messages and only the malformed one returns to the queue and, after maxReceiveCount, moves to the dead-letter queue.
